t1_read_text.detail: Live app STATE reads correctly: deck titles 'Not Loaded.' (x2), sampler BPM as a real edit value ('120.00'), status bar '32 Tracks, 1 hours 51 minutes, 818.4 MB' — all matching the pixels.

t2_enumerate.detail: 549 nodes: 141 buttons, 17 sliders, 8 radios, 4 combos, 6 edits — the ENTIRE custom-drawn performance chrome is annotated (names are developer IDs like 'WiFiSyncDetectButton', 'SelectFullArtworkButton': machine-usable, not user-facing labels). This REFUTES 'custom-drawn implies structural silence' for the second time in the campaign — the Windows twin of macOS Chess: the boundary is developer annotation, not rendering technology. Same rendering class as FL Studio (52 empty panes), opposite outcome.

t6_pictorial.detail: THE GAP, and it is the campaign's known silent class: the track-browser GRID. The channel declares the table's 11 column headers, then ZERO rows — while the screen lists the user's playlists and 11+ visible tracks with ratings. A naive consumer reads 'empty table'. Distinctive nuance vs OBS/FL: the view is SELF-INCONSISTENT in a detectable way (in-channel status bar says '32 Tracks' against an empty table; headers without rows) — a router can flag 'virtualized/unexposed list' from the view alone, but nothing DECLARES the rows unreadable, so it stays in the silent class by the campaign's standard.

measurements.notes: View 2003 tok vs 2584 fullscreen-window shot. Capture 1.5-1.8 s — the slowest bridge measured in the campaign (JUCE proxies each property; 549 nodes x several properties). The two-sided verdict is the value of this cell: (a) JUCE proves annotation can ride on a fully custom renderer (141 controls, states, values); (b) the one region it left out — the content grid — is exactly the silent-by-omission class, now seen in three variants (Qt anonymous container, Delphi named-empty panes, JUCE headers-without-rows). Round-1 bonus datum kept: the Upmgr updater dialog (also JUCE) showed the same shape in miniature — named headers ('Current Version', 'Update Version'), empty CustomControl cells. Ops note: one transient window died mid-enumeration and threw COMError on .Name — the stale-handle race again; enumeration loops must guard every property read.

runtime_verification.agreement: chrome and states: full agreement, value-exact. Track browser: DISAGREEMENT by omission (headers + '32 Tracks' in channel, zero rows vs 11+ on screen) — recorded as the silent class
